advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `browser_runner` consult `_PROVISION_ERROR`/`_PROVISION_ATTEMPTED` (mirroring `bpmn_harness`) so a failed provisioning is reported with the named error for the browser tier too.
evidence: tests/e2e/conftest.py:41: `_TOOLCHAIN_FIXTURES = frozenset({"bpmn_harness", "browser_runner"})`
tests/e2e/conftest.py:96-102: bpmn_harness consults `_PROVISION_ERROR` / `_PROVISION_ATTEMPTED` and re-runs the fallback
tests/e2e/conftest.py:130-134: browser_runner only checks `_have_node()` and `node_modules/playwright`, with no reference to `_PROVISION_ERROR` or `_PROVISION_ATTEMPTED`
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `_PROVISION` in conftest.py returns hits only at lines 44-98, none inside the browser_runner fixture (lines 124-162)
advisory.finding: `browser_runner` is listed in `_TOOLCHAIN_FIXTURES` (so its selection triggers collection-time provisioning) but its fixture body never checks `_PROVISION_ERROR` or `_PROVISION_ATTEMPTED`. When provisioning fails at collection time, `bpmn_harness` self-skips with the named provisioning error, while a browser test instead falls through to the generic `playwright not installed` skip and never runs the in-fixture fallback — the fix's promise that 'every failure names the step' is not honored for the browser tier.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `browser_runner`, after the node check, add the same guards used by `bpmn_harness`: `if _PROVISION_ERROR is not None: pytest.skip(f"e2e: {_PROVISION_ERROR}")` and an `if not _PROVISION_ATTEMPTED: provision_toolchain(_JS_DIR)` fallback.

evidence: _toolchain.py:119 `install = ["ci"] if (js_dir / "package-lock.json").is_file() else ["install"]`
test_toolchain_provisioning.py:42 `(js_dir / "package-lock.json").write_text('{"lockfileVersion":3}\n', ...)` — the helper unconditionally creates the lockfile
ABSENCE: no test constructs a js_dir with package.json but WITHOUT package-lock.json to assert `npm install` (not `npm ci`) is run
_toolchain.py:121-124 `# Re-check under the lock: a peer may have finished while this caller waited.` then `if not (js_dir / "node_modules").is_dir(): _run_step(...)`

test_toolchain_provisioning.py:166-177 _CONCURRENCY_STUB `ci|install` case is empty (`;;`) and only appends markers — it never `mkdir node_modules`, so the re-check condition stays true for both workers
test_toolchain_provisioning.py:211 asserts `ordered == ["start", "end", "start", "end"]` — proves serialization but requires BOTH installs to run, so it cannot exercise the peer-finished skip
advisory.finding: The `npm install` fallback branch of provision_toolchain (used when no package-lock.json exists) is never exercised: the _js_dir test helper always writes a package-lock.json, so every test hits the `npm ci` branch and the `else ["install"]` path has zero coverage.
merged_from: The under-lock re-check short-circuit in provision_toolchain (skip install/build when a peer already produced node_modules/the bundle) is not verified. The concurrency stub never creates node_modules, so both workers always run the install step and the re-check never short-circuits.
scenarios: A checkout/tree with no lockfile: a regression that dropped the else branch or ran `npm ci` (which errors without a lockfile) would not be caught

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an `actions/setup-node` step (pinned SHA + explicit `node-version`) before `make e2e-deps` so the e2e Node toolchain build is reproducible and not subject to runner-image drift.
evidence: `search_files` for `setup-node` in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml returned `(no matches)`
`if [ '${{ matrix.os }}' != 'macos-latest' ]; then make e2e-deps; fi` (line 475) invokes `npm ci && npm run build` with no preceding Node setup step
ABSENCE: no `uses: actions/setup-node@...` with a `node-version` pin anywhere in the workflow, so the Node version is whatever the runner image provides and can change without a repo change
advisory.finding: CI runs `npm ci` / `npm run build` (via `make e2e-deps`) without any `actions/setup-node` step pinning a Node version, so the toolchain build depends on the unpinned Node/npm that happens to ship in the GitHub-hosted runner image — a reproducibility/drift risk when the runner image updates.
scenarios: A GitHub runner image update bumps the default Node major version and the esbuild bundle build or `npm ci` engine check begins to fail or produce a different bundle, with no diff in the repo to explain it
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a pinned `actions/setup-node` step with an explicit `node-version` (or `node-version-file`) ahead of the `make e2e-deps` invocation, matching the version the harness's engines/lockfile expect.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Include the Node/npm version in the `~/.npm` cache key (or pin Node via setup-node whose own cache is version-aware) so the cache cannot be reused across incompatible toolchain versions.
evidence: `key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json') }}` (line 461)
`restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-` (line 463) will restore a stale cache when the lockfile hash changes
ABSENCE: cache key contains no Node/npm version component while no `setup-node` pins the version
advisory.finding: The `~/.npm` cache key hashes only `runner.os` + `tests/e2e/js/package-lock.json`, not the Node/npm version; combined with the unpinned runner Node, a Node/npm upgrade can reuse a cache produced by a different toolchain version.
scenarios: Runner image bumps Node; the OS-prefixed restore-key restores an npm cache built under the old Node, and native/optional deps mismatch
advisory.suggested_fix: Once Node is pinned via setup-node, either use setup-node's built-in npm caching or add the resolved Node version to the cache `key`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `e2e-deps` on `node` (not only `npm`), or make its invocation non-fatal, so a missing/incompatible Node self-skips as documented rather than failing the build.
evidence: `@if ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then ... exit 0; fi;` (lines 468-471) checks only npm
comment claims `Absent Node is not an error: the e2e tier is self-skipping ... leave that decision to pytest rather than failing the build here` (Makefile:466-467) yet the guard never checks `node`
`cd tests/e2e/js && npm ci && npm run build` runs the esbuild bundle which needs `node`
advisory.finding: The `e2e-deps` Makefile target guards only on `command -v npm` but the harness also requires `node`; on a host with npm-but-no-node (or a broken Node install) the target proceeds to `npm ci && npm run build` and can fail the build rather than skip cleanly as the comment promises.
scenarios: A checkout/CI host where npm resolves but node does not (or node is a version esbuild rejects): `make e2e-deps` fails non-zero and, in CI, `make e2e-deps` runs unconditionally (no `|| true`), failing the whole job
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the guard to `if ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo skipping; exit 0; fi`, and/or invoke it in CI as `make e2e-deps || true` consistent with the self-skip contract.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Move the completeness fast-path check in provision_toolchain inside `_install_lock`, and gate the re-check on a completion sentinel (not merely `node_modules` dir existence) so a peer's in-progress `npm ci` cannot be mistaken for a finished install.
evidence: Shared resource: `if (js_dir / "node_modules").is_dir() and bundle.is_file(): return` (_toolchain.py:108-109) — the on-disk node_modules dir and dist/roundtrip.mjs, gitignored and absent on a cold checkout (tests/e2e/js/.gitignore; list_directory shows no node_modules/ or dist/).

Two concurrent executors: xdist worker PROCESSES under `pytest -n 4 --dist worksteal`; each is a fresh interpreter so `_PROVISION_ATTEMPTED` (conftest.py:46) is per-process and every worker calls provision_toolchain (conftest.py:79 collection hook and conftest.py:100 fixture fallback).

Interleaving window — WRITE: worker A holds the lock and runs `_run_step(f"npm {install[0]}", ...)` (_toolchain.py:123); `npm ci` deletes and recreates node_modules, creating the directory early and populating it over ~90-120s. READ: worker B executes the UNLOCKED `(js_dir / "node_modules").is_dir()` at _toolchain.py:108 and sees the directory present.

Sibling accessor + its guard: the SAME check is repeated INSIDE `with _install_lock(js_dir):` at _toolchain.py:120-122 (`if not (js_dir / "node_modules").is_dir():`), establishing that this resource's install-time accessors are meant to be serialized by the flock — the line-108 twin omits that guard.

Concrete harm: corrupted-invariant / double-processing — worker B early-returns with node_modules only partially populated, then the fixture runs `subprocess.run([node, str(_BUNDLE)], ...)` (conftest.py:106-113) against missing dependencies, yielding a hard harness AssertionError ('harness produced no output' / import failure) rather than the intended skip — the opposite of the diagnosable outcome the change set out to guarantee.
dropped.finding: `provision_toolchain`'s fast-path completeness check reads the shared `node_modules`/`dist` state OUTSIDE the install lock, so a worker can early-return on a peer's in-progress `npm ci` (which recreates node_modules early) plus a stale bundle, and then run the harness against a half-installed node_modules.
scenarios: Cold `tests/e2e/js` (node_modules absent) with a leftover `dist/roundtrip.mjs` from a prior build, run under `-n 4 --dist worksteal` with no `make e2e-deps` pre-step: the first worker's in-progress `npm ci` recreates node_modules while a second worker's unlocked fast-path sees dir+bundle and returns early.
dropped.suggested_fix: Perform the `node_modules.is_dir() and bundle.is_file()` check under the lock, and have a successful install write a completion marker (e.g. touch a `.provisioned` file after `npm run build`) that the fast-path tests instead of the presence of the node_modules directory, since `npm ci` creates that directory long before the install completes.
